_comment: Which golden rules are promoted out of their chapter and into the two headline
tiers of the viva deck. Read by tools/viva-extract.php; the order here is the
order they appear in GOLDEN-RULES.md and in the deck, so it is rehearsal order,
not chapter order.
This is the one editorial judgement in an otherwise generated pipeline. The twelve
run language first, then the two things every PHP interview in this market
actually tests: whether you can be trusted with user input, and whether you know
why the page is slow. Nothing about frameworks appears until the end, because a
candidate who can explain injection and the N+1 gets asked about Laravel next,
and a candidate who can only explain Laravel does not.
Note the shape of this list against the Kafka one. There the questions that decide
the interview are model questions, because no advert asks for Kafka alone. Here
the adverts ask for PHP directly and at length, so the twelve are the concrete
claims a technical round opens with — and half of them are security or the
database, which is where these interviews actually spend their time.
The senior six are the operating rules. They are not harder; they are the ones you
only know from having deployed something and watched it misbehave, which is
exactly the gap between the CV and the second interview. The last of them is the
gestionale rule, kept because in Emilia-Romagna it is not a niche.
Every entry must be a slug that tools/viva-extract.php --candidates prints. A slug
that no longer exists is reported as a WARNING rather than silently dropped.
